cells.tense: You are in the middle of an ending, and you are not rushing it.
cells.ask: Finish one thing all the way this week — the last message, the last box, the last payment — and let it be done.
cells.core:
You can tell when something has actually run its course, and you act on it. An ending shows up and you don't argue with it. You close the account, you say the last thing, you let it be over — then you let the next one arrive on its own schedule.

That's rarer than starting things. Ending cleanly takes feeling: a clear read on what's done and the nerve to stop feeding it. You're not managing this tonight. You're here while it happens, doing the plain work, and afterward the day goes quieter than it was. That quiet is what you were after, not the price of it.
cells.sheetLine: You can end a thing without wrecking it.
cells.verb: letting what's finished end so what's next can begin
cells.place: where you become what you already are

cells.tense: You are already living past the ending that hasn't happened yet.
cells.ask: When you catch yourself planning the exit, put both feet in one plan for a week — and notice one person you keep rehearsing the goodbye with.
cells.core:
Something gets going and part of you is already at its funeral. You can see the ending before it arrives, so you move first. Quit before it goes stale, cut before it fades, call it freedom and feel the floor drop anyway. The next version is where you live. This one keeps getting left.

The clear read on what's finished is good. In front of an ending that hasn't happened, it turns into pre-empting everything, and nothing gets long enough to become real. The fix is a person, not a plan: stay close to one of them while you do it, and let the ending keep its own calendar.
cells.sheetLine: You end things early so they can't end on you.

cells.tense: You have stayed put where the ground moved, and you have not moved with it.
cells.ask: Do one small thing this week that's yours alone, and notice what it points toward — the call, the paperwork, the box.
cells.core:
Leaving a thing that's over is a skill you've had. You've said the last word before and put the box out, let a season finish without pretending it was still going, and that took a read anyone could trust.

It isn't running now. You're steady and present and you don't make a fuss, and under all of it something has stopped and you're keeping it going by standing there. Loyalty can be the shape of it. Keeping your word can be the shape of it. What's missing isn't nerve. It's a direction — nothing has asked your feet to move yet, so they haven't. One thing you care about, done this week, gives them one, and nothing has to feel right first.

cells.tense: You are already in the middle of a change you haven't named out loud.
cells.ask: Tell one person in your own words what you've quietly stopped doing — and what you've quietly started — this week.
cells.core:
Something in you is already letting go. A habit, a tie, a version of yourself you used to introduce people to — it's been fading while you weren't watching. You call it a busy stretch. You call it being tired. Meanwhile you've stopped calling, stopped showing up to the thing, started dressing differently, started answering differently, and you haven't said so once.

The move has been happening under the surface. What hasn't happened is you claiming it, and that's the reason it reads as drift instead of a choice. Say what's ending and what's already started. You're standing on ground you thought you were losing.
cells.sheetLine: You've already changed. You're calling it a phase.
